root_cause.text: `tpm2_read_public()` in the TPM2 sessions code leaks the `tpm_buf` page allocation because it calls `tpm_buf_init()` but misses `tpm_buf_destroy()` on the `name_size()` error return path and on the normal success return path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);` before `return name_size_alg;` when `name_size_alg < 0`, and also adds `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);` just before the final successful return; the commit message explicitly says these two exit paths previously failed to destroy the buffer, causing a page allocation leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a cleanup omission in `tpm2_read_public()` by destroying the TPM buffer before returning when `name_size()` fails.
intent_record.what: In `tpm2_read_public()`, the negative `name_size_alg` error check was expanded from a simple early return to a block that first calls `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` and then returns the error; the surrounding logic was otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: If `name_size()` fails, the function now cleans up the allocated TPM buffer before exiting, preventing a resource leak on this error path while preserving the same returned error code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the TPM buffer before returning from `tpm2_read_public()` to fix a memory/resource leak.
intent_record.what: A call to `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);` was added immediately before the `return name_size_alg;` statement in `tpm2_read_public()`, after the `memcpy()` call.
intent_record.how: This ensures the temporary TPM buffer is released before the function exits, preventing a resource leak on the normal successful return path.

grouping_result.intent: Free the TPM buffer before returning from `tpm2_read_public()` to fix a memory/resource leak.

consistency_review.core_intent: Free the TPM buffer before returning from tpm2_read_public() to fix a memory/resource leak.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the reported root cause: `tpm2_read_public()` was leaking the `tpm_buf` allocation due to missing `tpm_buf_destroy()` on both the error and success return paths.

candidates.rationale: This early return exits tpm2_read_public() after tpm_buf_init() without calling tpm_buf_destroy(), directly causing the page allocation leak when name_size() fails.
This normal success return also leaves the function without destroying buf, so the TPM buffer allocation remains leaked on the successful path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This return path in tpm2_read_public() exits after tpm_buf_init() without a corresponding tpm_buf_destroy(), so when name_size() fails the allocated TPM buffer page is leaked.
This normal success return path also leaves tpm2_read_public() without calling tpm_buf_destroy(), causing the TPM buffer allocation to remain leaked on successful completion.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the relevant cleanup and does not match the leak root cause. It calls `tpm_buf_init(&buf, TPM2_ST_NO_SESSIONS, TPM2_CC_READ_PUBLIC);` and on the transmit error path it explicitly frees the buffer: `if (rc) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return tpm_ret_to_err(rc); }`. It also destroys the buffer on the range-check failure paths: `if (offset + 4 > tpm_buf_length(&buf)) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }` and `if (rc != name_size_alg) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }` and `if (offset + rc > tpm_buf_length(&buf)) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }`. The only path that returns without `tpm_buf_destroy()` is the final success return `return name_size_alg;`, but in this commit the vulnerability described is a page-allocation leak from missing `tpm_buf_destroy()` on success/error paths. Since the function body shown is already a reworked implementation with explicit frees on error and no missing cleanup in the relevant control paths, the vulnerable construct is not present here and the fix is already applied.
